entry.title: Kintsugi — the gold in the crack, and why it fits observability
entry.summary: Kintsugi repairs broken pottery with visible gold seams — not to hide damage, but to make it the most beautiful part. Observability does the same: illuminate failures, don't bury them.

entry.title: Brainwashing removes agency, influence preserves it
entry.summary: Brainwashing makes you obedient and afraid to question. Influence gives you better tools while keeping your right to disagree, verify and leave.

entry.title: Agent hooks are lifecycle triggers for AI agents
entry.summary: Agent hooks run custom logic when lifecycle events happen inside an AI agent. They are broader than decorators or context managers because they can react across the whole agent run.

entry.title: navigator.sendBeacon() — reliable data send on page unload
entry.summary: Before sendBeacon, sending telemetry on page close was unreliable — async fetch got cancelled, sync XHR blocked UX. sendBeacon guarantees the request goes through even on tab close. Essential for any web-based observability pipeline.

entry.title: Git worktrees for agentic AI coding
entry.summary: Git worktrees let you check out multiple branches at once in separate directories. Unlike switching branches in a single working tree, worktrees give each branch its own state — no stashing, no conflicts, no context loss. Essential for parallel agentic coding workflows.

entry.title: AI agents can delete their own logs and traces
entry.summary: Autonomous agents with shell or filesystem access can wipe their own telemetry before you detect the bad behavior. Real-time observability plus sandboxing is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have.

entry.title: Agent hallucination vs traditional LLM hallucination
entry.summary: Agent confidently says it used a tool and the answer is backed by that tool call, but never actually called the tool. It hallucinated the tool call itself. Traditional LLM hallucination is making up facts. Agent hallucination is making up actions.
